title: Question 1.4
statement_text: Is $\Delta(1,2,2)$ a hero in oriented complete multipartite graphs?
context_text: Digraphs have no digons, loops or multi-arcs. The dichromatic number of a digraph is the minimum number of sets in a partition of its vertices into sets inducing acyclic subdigraphs. A digraph is $H$-free if it has no induced subdigraph isomorphic to $H$, and $H$ is a hero in a class $\mathcal{C}$ if the $H$-free digraphs of $\mathcal{C}$ have bounded dichromatic number. An oriented complete multipartite graph is an orientation of a complete multipartite graph. $TT_k$ is the transitive tournament on $k$ vertices; for tournaments $H_1,H_2$, $\Delta(1,H_1,H_2)$ is obtained from disjoint copies of $H_1$ and $H_2$ plus a vertex $x$, with all arcs from $x$ to $H_1$, from $H_1$ to $H_2$, and from $H_2$ to $x$; integers stand for transitive tournaments, so $\Delta(1,2,2)=\Delta(1,TT_2,TT_2)$ is a 5-vertex tournament. $H_1\Rightarrow H_2$ is the disjoint union of $H_1$ and $H_2$ with all arcs from $H_1$ to $H_2$. Berger et al. characterized heroes in tournaments; since oriented complete multipartite graphs contain all tournaments, a hero there must be a hero in tournaments. The paper shows that $\Delta(1,2,C_3)$, $\Delta(1,C_3,2)$, $\Delta(1,2,3)$ and $\Delta(1,3,2)$ are not heroes in oriented complete multipartite graphs (disproving a conjecture of Aboulker, Charbit and Naserasr), and that $K_1$, $H_1\Rightarrow H_2$ and $\Delta(1,1,H_1)$ are heroes whenever $H_1,H_2$ are. Hence heroes in this class are characterized up to the status of $\Delta(1,2,2)$: if it is not a hero, the heroes are exactly those generated by these three rules; if it is, $\Delta(1,2,2)$ must be added as a base case. A remark in the final version states that, after submission, Walczak proved that non-interlaced ordered graphs have unbounded chromatic number, which together with a theorem of the paper implies that $\Delta(1,2,2)$ is not a hero, though the authors did not yet claim this as a theorem since that proof was not yet published.
paper_title: Heroes in oriented complete multipartite graphs

title: Conjecture 5.1
statement_text: For every oriented forest $F$, every transitive tournament is a hero in $Forb_{ind}(F)$.
context_text: This conjecture, posed by Aboulker, Charbit, and Naserasr as an oriented analogue of the well-known Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture, concerns dichromatic boundedness in $F$-free digraphs. It is known that if $F$ is not a disjoint union of oriented stars, the only possible heroes in $Forb_{ind}(F)$ are transitive tournaments, and the conjecture has been verified for oriented stars.
paper_contribution: The paper proves Theorems 5.2 and 5.3 establishing new partial results towards this conjecture in the setting of oriented forests, building on the known reduction to trees.
paper_title: Heroes in oriented complete multipartite graphs

title: Question 5.4
statement_text: Let $H$ and $F$ be digraphs such that $\Delta(1,1,H)$ is a hero in $Forb_{ind}(F)$ and $H$ is a hero in $Forb_{ind}(K_{1}+F)$. Then $\Delta(1,1,H)$ is a hero in $Forb_{ind}(K_{1}+F)$.
context_text: Digraphs have no digons, loops or multi-arcs. The dichromatic number of a digraph is the minimum number of sets in a partition of its vertices into sets inducing acyclic subdigraphs. A digraph is $H$-free if it has no induced subdigraph isomorphic to $H$; $Forb_{ind}(F)$ is the class of $F$-free digraphs, and $H$ is a hero in a class $\mathcal{C}$ if the $H$-free digraphs of $\mathcal{C}$ have bounded dichromatic number. $K_1$ is the one-vertex digraph and $G_1+G_2$ denotes disjoint union; $\bar{K}_t$ is the digraph on $t$ vertices with no arc, $TT_k$ the transitive tournament on $k$ vertices, and $\vec{P}_3$ the directed path on 3 vertices. $\Delta(1,1,H)$ is obtained from a copy of $H$ plus two vertices $x,y$ with the arc $xy$, all arcs from $y$ to $H$ and all arcs from $H$ to $x$. Oriented complete multipartite graphs are exactly $Forb_{ind}(K_1+TT_2)$. The paper proves the analogous transfer statement for $H_1\Rightarrow H_2$ (disjoint union with all arcs from $H_1$ to $H_2$): if $H_1\Rightarrow H_2$ is a hero in $Forb_{ind}(F)$ and $H_1,H_2$ are heroes in $Forb_{ind}(K_1+F)$, then $H_1\Rightarrow H_2$ is a hero in $Forb_{ind}(K_1+F)$. Knowing heroes in $Forb_{ind}(F)$ does not in general help with $Forb_{ind}(K_1+F)$ (every digraph is a hero in $Forb_{ind}(K_1)$ and in $Forb_{ind}(TT_2)$, while very few are heroes in $Forb_{ind}(K_1+TT_2)$), and heroes in $Forb_{ind}(\bar{K}_t)$ were shown to coincide with heroes in tournaments by a hard proof. A positive answer to this question would show that heroes in $Forb_{ind}(F)$ for $F=\bar{K}_t+TT_2$ or $F=\bar{K}_t+\vec{P}_3$ are the same as in oriented complete multipartite graphs (up to the status of $\Delta(1,2,2)$).
paper_title: Heroes in oriented complete multipartite graphs
